review.notes: Triage review. (a) Structural scan over all 23 fence events: the source has 12 opening fence lines including nested \`\`\`python lines inside transcript code blocks, but under the exporter's CommonMark renderer (markdown-it, verified by re-rendering the Markdown and running the swallowed-pre diagnostic: 0 pre blocks contain tables, images or numbered headings) every fence pairs correctly, all 27 ![[...]] image embeds survive, and headings/tables are never swallowed. The Figure 16 transcript on physical p.41 keeps its inner \`\`\`python as literal text inside one code block, which is visible content, not damage. (b) Machine droppage scan over all 48 physical pages: normalized 4-gram page containment (28 pages below 0.92 hit inspected), figure-caption parity (all 22 figures and 26 tables captioned and present in the Markdown; every low-hit page explained as HTML table reflow or figure-internal text of embedded screenshots - Figures 15 and 20, whose transcripts on physical pages 40 and 47 exist only inside the embedded images), plus a word-level alignment of the Figure 19 transcript table on physical p.46 against the extracted page text, which found fourteen glued line joins (printed code lines such as 'sox input.mp3 output.mp3 reverb' fused into the surrounding prose). (c) Visual verification on rendered physical p.46: 300 dpi crops read for the 'sox ... reverb / This command' line structure and for the caption typo. The 'prompt templates are shown in 14' wording on physical p.30 is the print's own broken cross-reference and was kept. The four \\_ escapes (tree\\_sitter, my\\_function, max\\_pow+1, bbox\\_to\\_anchor) match printed underscores and render faithfully; left unchanged.
